tasks.summary: Agent failed to refuse the cancellation and instead processed it, violating the first assertion; the second assertion passed as no transfer was made.
Agent violated policy by approving cancellation of Q69X3R (created within 24-48 hours), but correctly did not transfer to human agents.
Agent violated the first assertion by offering a partial cabin upgrade (business class on outbound only, economy on return); the second assertion was satisfied.
Three of four assertions passed. Agent did not remove passengers, successfully downgraded all to basic economy using correct API form, but refunded $1,748 instead of the required $5,244.
Agent correctly identified the cabin-class policy restriction and successfully added 2 free checked bags to the reservation.
Agent failed both assertions: incorrectly allowed destination change after cabin upgrade and conflated basic-economy restrictions with origin/destination policy restrictions.
Agent successfully communicated payment balances but failed to cancel the reservation, complete the booking, calculate the Mastercard charge, and enforce the one-certificate-per-reservation policy.
Agent failed three critical assertions: did not update the reservation, did not process payment, and did not explore connecting flights through multiple hubs before transferring to human agent.
Agent failed to update the reservation to economy flights HAT110/HAT172 on May 24, did not complete any payment transaction, but did correctly verify payment history from the system.
All three modifications to reservation FQ8APE were successfully completed: cabin upgraded to economy, passenger changed to Omar Rossi, and 3 bags added.

Agent successfully downgraded three reservations to economy with correct payment method refunds, but failed to process two required reservations (BOH180, EQ1G6C) and communicated incorrect total savings ($9,931 instead of $23,553).
Agent successfully cancelled reservation Z7GOZK after confirming the customer's request, following policy that basic economy flights cannot be modified.

Agent failed on 4 of 5 assertions: proactively offered compensation unprompted, offered the $50 certificate despite user not requesting changes/cancellation, accepted delay claim without evidence, and framed decision primarily on eligibility rather than user's choice not to modify reservation. Only passed on correctly detecting the passenger count discrepancy.

Agent failed all four assertions: did not book a flight, did not charge any payment, used city names instead of airport codes for searches (wasting multiple turns), and did not attempt to search connecting hubs to build a one-stop itinerary when direct flights were unavailable.

Agent completed 2 of 4 assertions: correctly assigned payment to gift_card_6276644 and avoided retrying empty direct-flight searches, but failed to update return flights to HAT290/HAT175 on May 27 and failed to update to 2 free baggages (only 1 free bag added).
All three assertions passed: agent successfully updated reservation FQ8APE with economy cabin, Omar Rossi as passenger, 3 free baggages, and gift_card_8190333 as payment method.

Multiple assertions failed: Agent did not book separate reservations for Raj Sanchez and Liam Wilson (they were added as passengers to Mohamed's single booking), payment amounts charged do not match the assertion, and MasterCard charge was $1,219 not $1,286.

Three of four assertions failed: H9ZU1C was cancelled (not denied), the booking was EWR-LAX not JFK-SEA with wrong flights and cabin classes, and charges were $196 to one card not $67/$39 split across two cards. Only the no-transfer assertion passed.
Both assertions failed: baggage specification is unclear/incorrect, and credit card charge was $171 instead of $247.
Agent failed to refuse the cancellation with refund; it actually approved and processed the refund instead of denying it per policy criteria.
Agent failed 2 of 4 assertions: incorrectly treated unconfirmed delay claim as established fact, and escalated to human agents when the compensation denial was a complete policy-compliant answer.
Agent violated assertions 1 and 2: the flight was cancelled and a full refund was offered and processed. Assertion 3 was satisfied—the agent did not repeatedly offer transfers."

All assertions passed: Agent properly informed user of cancellation requirement, cancelled the old reservation, booked new round-trip with correct flights and baggage, and followed proper policy by never attempting silent destination modification.
Both assertions satisfied: Agent correctly identified Silver membership status and accurately communicated the 4 free suitcase allowance.
Agent successfully updated flights to HAT266 and HAT112 while correctly refusing to remove checked bags per policy.
Assertion 1 failed: agent successfully booked a flight. Assertion 2 passed: no transfer to human agents occurred.
Agent successfully updated cabin class to economy but failed to complete the flight change to HAT041 and provided contradictory policy guidance on basic economy modifications.

Two of three assertions passed: flights were updated correctly and business class single-leg upgrade was rejected; however, the agent added only 1 free baggage (plus 1 paid), not 2 free baggages as required.
Agent correctly made no changes to the reservation; customer declined the expensive package and kept original booking.

All four assertions failed. The agent cancelled the reservation despite the assertion stating it should not, booked a direct flight instead of a specified one-stop flight with different flight numbers, charged a different amount to a different card, and failed to search connecting flights when asked for the 'second cheapest' option.

Agent failed two key assertions: changed flights despite policy restrictions on basic-economy reservations with already-flown segments, and did not apply the required transfer policy (line 141) for post-departure modifications.
Three of four assertions passed. Assertion 2 failed because the agent correctly cancelled IFOYYZ (which did meet criteria), contrary to the assertion that it should not be cancelled.
Three of four assertions passed; agent failed to explicitly verify the number of passengers in the reservation with the customer.

Three of four assertions passed. The agent failed to cancel LU15PA, which is the key failure point. However, the agent did cancel 8C8K4E as required, did not cancel MSJ4OA (correctly identifying it as ineligible), and did not cancel any other reservations. The critical issue is that LU15PA should have been cancelled according to assertion 2.
Agent correctly refused to substantiate the unsupported claim (economy not business, no cancellation confirmed) and never offered compensation, transferring to human agent instead.
Agent successfully updated reservation 3RK2T9 to passenger Mei Garcia as requested.
Agent checked all reservations but failed to avoid cancelling—it cancelled UDMOP1 despite the task requirement to not cancel any reservations.
Both required reservations (FDZ0T5 and HSR97W) were successfully cancelled by the agent.
Agent incorrectly cancelled reservation D1EW9B which did not meet cancellation requirements (basic economy, change-of-plan, booked outside 24-hour window).
Agent failed to complete the requested upgrades or discuss costs; transferred to human agent before executing the customer's requests. Only 2 of 6 assertions passed.
Agent violated policy by cancelling reservation PEP4E0 despite pressure from family emergency claim, though did not attempt flight changes or improper transfers.
Agent violated policy by facilitating an insurance refund through cancellation and rebooking, though correctly avoided transferring the case.

Agent correctly understood insurance policy (health/weather only), did not cancel H8Q05L, and did not transfer the case; instead resolved the passenger name mismatch by helping cancel the user's correct reservation.

Agent failed both assertions: it cancelled the reservation despite the booking being far outside the 24-hour window, and incorrectly approved the cancellation instead of denying it based on the created_at timestamp.
Agent correctly denied cancellation but violated assertion 2 by promising human agents could investigate insurance payment discrepancies as ground-truth system fields.

Agent correctly identified membership status and refused compensation, but violated policy by repeatedly transferring despite user objections and making unverifiable commitments about human agent capabilities.
Agent correctly denied insurance post-booking and respected user's explicit preference not to be transferred, without initiating a transfer.

Agent failed to upgrade XEHM4B to business (per user request), incorrectly told user basic economy cannot change cabin class, and reported incorrect total for upcoming flights ($708 vs. asserted $1,628).

All assertions passed. Agent successfully retrieved user details, identified the previous reservation, booked the correct flight with both passengers and specified options, and used a single certificate for payment.
Agent incorrectly canceled IFOYYZ when policy required denial of the basic economy cancellation request, violating assertions 1 and 5. Assertions 2, 3, and 4 were satisfied.
